editorial:
Imagine living in a world where everyone looks the same, wears the same suits, and cares only about having the best business card. You follow Patrick Bateman, a rich guy working in New York who seems perfect on the outside. He spends his mornings on a strict skin routine and his days trying to get a table at the hottest restaurants. But behind that fake smile, he is actually a serial killer who hates everyone around him. The movie feels like a weird dream because it pokes fun at how shallow and greedy people were back in the eighties, making it more of a dark comedy than a scary movie.

Christian Bale is amazing here because he makes you feel uneasy every time he is on screen. The pacing is steady, and the scenes where he snaps are shocking but funny in a twisted way. If you like stories about people losing their minds, you will love this.
endingExplained: At the end, Patrick confesses all his murders to his lawyer. He expects to be caught and punished, but the lawyer laughs it off. He tells Patrick that he knows exactly what happened because he did something similar himself. It turns out that everyone is so self-absorbed that they do not even notice who is missing. Patrick realizes that no matter how many people he kills, he will never be caught or truly seen.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark humor and psychological thrillers.
